newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU's van Miert to check German TV alliance-report.
newsitem.headline: EU's van Miert to check German TV alliance-report.

text.p: European Union Commissioner Karel van Miert plans to review a German digital television alliance to see if it poses a threat to competition, the newsweekly Der Spiegel said on Saturday.

The "critical point" for van Miert was the participation of Deutsche Telekom AG in an alliance with media giants Bertelsmann and the Kirch Group, the magazine said in an advance copy of an article due to appear on Monday.
Telekom operates Germany's dominant cable system TV system.

ANGA, an organisation of private cable system operators, had already filed a complaint with the European Commission, saying that the alliance represented a "massive threat to competition," Der Spiegel said.
The head of Germany's cartel office, Dieter Wolf, has also expessed doubts about the plan to combine Kirch's DF-1 digital TV with Premiere, a pay-per-view broadcaster in which each owns a stake.
But Bertelsmann chief executive Michael Dornemann said earlier this month after meeting van Miert that he did not expect any problems gaining EU approval.
